solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Crooked person, one ending in slammer?

definitions.text: Crooked person, one ending in slammer?

parts.words: Crooked person, one ending in slammer?
parts.note: a crook who is caught finishes up behind bars, in the slammer, which is slang for jail

explanation.surface: A description of a dishonest character who comes to grief.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: someone crooked who ends up locked in a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A convicted crook held in jail is an inmate, a captive of the prison system.

clue.text: Improve image of soldiers on move

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is the usual abbreviation for a body of soldiers
to move someone emotionally is to touch them

explanation.surface: A photographer polishes a picture of troops on manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' reads as marching about, but it means stirring the feelings; 'on' simply places one piece next to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers touch up a picture with small edits to make it look better.

clue.text: Tots on either side of net in playing this?

definitions.text: Tots on either side of net in playing this?

parts.words: Tots on either side of net in playing this?
parts.note: small children playing a racket game across a net, with a pun on tots being short

explanation.surface: Little children face each other over a net in some game.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is a scaled-down form of the racket sport for youngsters; its first word also describes the little players.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini version of lawn tennis with smaller court and rackets, designed to introduce young children to the sport.

clue.text: Proud parent back home with award

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for being at home from right to left

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: A mother or father beams on returning home with a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proud' points to the myth: the definition is a figure from Greek legend, not an everyday boastful parent.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Niobe boasted of her many children over Leto's two, and lost them all for her pride.

clue.text: Right means of escape in retreat

parts.note: an egress is a way out

explanation.surface: An escape route that is the proper way to fall back.
explanation.definitionFit: To go backwards or revert to an earlier state is to fall back, the same movement as a retreat.

clue.text: Physicist's bilingual parents going in different directions

indicators.note: the two parents travel opposite ways, so the English one is read right to left while the other runs forwards

parts.note: MA is mum, one parent in English
the clue wants one parent in each language, so the other is French pere, father

explanation.surface: A scientist whose mother and father speak two languages and have split up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bilingual parents' means one in English (MA) and one in French (PERE); 'going in different directions' reverses MA to AM and leaves PERE as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre-Marie Ampere was the French scientist after whom the unit of electric current is named.

clue.text: Sweet food getting left — it's really good

parts.note: angelica is a candied plant stem used on cakes

explanation.surface: A dessert that has been abandoned turns out to be delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as abandoned, but it just gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintly or heavenly in goodness, like an angel; extreme virtue is the sense.

clue.text: Letter from abroad with a lot of acidity

parts.note: pH is the scale on which acidity is measured
a pH reading of one, I in Roman numerals, means very strongly acidic

explanation.surface: Some foreign correspondence that tastes rather sour.
explanation.walkthrough: A pH of 1 is extremely acidic, so 'a lot of acidity' gives PH plus I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: Phi is the twenty-first character of the Greek alphabet, a letter used abroad.

clue.text: Fixing equipment on board

definitions.meaning: ... an election or match is fixing its result dishonestly
a ship's ropes, masts and sails make up its ...

explanation.surface: Repairing gear aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigging means both dishonest fixing of an outcome and the ropes and spars of a sailing ship.

clue.text: Unqualified yob wearing hot pants on the way out

indicators.note: British slang pants means rubbish, so the word hot is poorly assembled and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a rough is a hooligan or yob; wearing places him after the jumbled letters he has on
something going is departing or dying out

explanation.surface: A lout in skimpy shorts is leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot pants' looks like clothing, but 'pants' is the anagram signal, turning HOT into THO.
explanation.definitionFit: Unqualified praise or a thoroughgoing reform is complete and absolute, with no reservations.

clue.text: A loose woman in the family

parts.note: to loose a knot is to untie it

explanation.surface: A promiscuous female relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' looks like an adjective about the woman, but it is the verb meaning set free.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a female relative, a parent's sister.

clue.text: Catholic chosen to save canon's face, I see

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe within, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: the elect are the chosen

indicators.note: the face of something is its front, so take the opening letter

parts.note: IC sounds like I see when the letters are spoken

explanation.surface: A Roman Catholic selected to rescue a churchman's reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catholic' with a small c means wide-ranging, not the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower-case catholic tastes are broad and all-embracing, drawn from many sources.

clue.text: Financial record of our client going astray

indicators.note: letters wandering off course end up rearranged

explanation.surface: A client's bank statement has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterfoil is the stub kept from a cheque or receipt as proof of a payment.

clue.text: Miscues the shot, finding the score

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or wrecked, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A snooker player fluffs a shot and looks at the scoreboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' and 'score' suggest sport, but the score is written music.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical score is the printed notation for a piece, the pages a musician reads from.

clue.text: Return of stupid arithmetician, say, in warm period

indicators.note: a return goes back, so the word for stupid is read in reverse

parts.note: dim means dull-witted
someone who sums is jokingly a summer

explanation.surface: A foolish mathematician comes back during the hot weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' turns DIM into MID; 'say' flags SUMMER as an invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: Midsummer is the height of the season around the June solstice, the hottest stretch of the year.

clue.text: Yorkshire runner catching golf drive

indicators.note: one piece catches the other, holding it inside

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, and a runner is a river in crosswords
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An athlete from the north of England hits a long golf shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' and 'drive' are both sporting, but the runner is a river and drive is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive in the sense of an inner compulsion or strong desire is an urge.

clue.text: E.g. pen's tip of steel lacking in colour

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

parts.note: wan means pale

explanation.surface: A writing pen's steel nib is dull and colourless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool but is a female swan.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen is the female of the swan, as a cob is the male.

clue.text: Cover popular musician's sound

indicators.note: the clue asks for how the musician's name is heard

parts.note: a rapper is a performer of rap, a popular music style

explanation.surface: A sleeve for a hip-hop artist's recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapper is a covering, such as paper round a sweet.

clue.text: Readily opt to change cosmetic lotion?

indicators.note: changing the letters puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A shopper is quick to switch skin creams.
explanation.definitionFit: A depilatory is a hair-removing cream; the question mark admits it is only one kind of beauty product.

clue.text: Old coin in wetland, north in gorge

indicators.note: the second in places the boggy area and the compass point inside

parts.note: to pig is to gorge on food
a fen is a marsh

explanation.surface: A lost coin turns up in a marsh up north, in a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gorge' looks like a ravine, but it is the verb meaning eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: The pfennig was a small German coin, a hundredth of a mark, replaced by the euro.

clue.text: Dish with starters of kimchi in noodle soup

indicators.note: in places the opening letters inside the soup

parts.note: ramen is a Japanese noodle soup

indicators.note: starters, plural, means the first two letters

explanation.surface: A Korean side dish served with Japanese soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' is plural: take KI, the first two letters of 'kimchi'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramekin is a small baking dish for one portion.

clue.text: Widespread drug consumption one's seen in parlour

parts.note: mass, as in mass appeal, means widespread
E is ecstasy
use is consumption

explanation.surface: Rampant drug-taking in a parlour.
explanation.walkthrough: The parlour is a massage parlour.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseuse is a woman who gives massages, the professional working in a massage parlour.

clue.text: I'm leaving mum's fishy foodstuff

parts.note: ta-ra is a British informal goodbye
ma is mum

explanation.surface: Someone saying goodbye leaves their mother's fish paste.
explanation.walkthrough: TARA is northern English for 'goodbye'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarama is salted carp or cod roe, the base of taramasalata.

clue.text: Sign showing where Barbie's affections go?

parts.note: the destination word, as in going to someone
Ken is the boyfriend doll of Barbie

explanation.surface: An indicator of where a doll's love lies.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbie's affections go TO KEN, her doll boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is an outward sign or symbol, as in a token of esteem.

clue.text: Online comments criticise engaging staff for game

indicators.note: engaging means taking on or holding, so the staff go inside

parts.note: posts are comments made online
to man is to staff
to knock is to criticise

explanation.surface: Web critics attack a company's hiring.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman's knock is a party kissing game.
explanation.definitionFit: Postman's knock is a children's party game in which letters are delivered in exchange for kisses.

clue.text: Card game

definitions.meaning: a ... card in a mobile phone

explanation.definitionFit: SIM names both the phone's identity chip card and a genre of simulation games.

clue.text: Royal put on proper coat

indicators.note: put on means placed after, as the royal piece comes behind

parts.note: prim means prudishly proper
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A royal person wears an appropriate overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' is a layer of paint, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is the first layer of paint applied to prepare a surface.

clue.text: Traps fish in the drink

parts.note: gins are snares for game
a ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler snares fish in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' looks like slang for the sea, but it is the definition: a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin sling is a cocktail of gin, sweetened water and flavouring.
